newsitem.title: USA: ISSUER FOCUS - San Antonio, Texas electric & gas.
newsitem.headline: ISSUER FOCUS - San Antonio, Texas electric & gas.

text.p: Tuesday's expected $486 million San Antonio, Texas, electric and gas system bond sale will allow the city-owned utility to lock in attractive borrowing rates while preparing itself for the competition industry deregulation will bring, an official there said.
Donald Thomas, secretary-treasurer of the utility, City Public Service, said it will issue $350 million of new money bonds, accompanied by about $131 million of advance refunding bonds.
The refunding's total could fluctuate depending on market conditions, he said. PaineWebber Inc. will head the syndicate.

San Antonio historically has tried to achieve 5.0 percent net present value savings on its refundings, but with many of its higher-rate issues already refunded, the target this time is at least 3.0 percent, Thomas said.
"We'll achieve a little higher than that," he said.

The bond issue continues the utility's strategy of selling debt for new projects or improvements when long-term rates are low, and continuing to replace older, higher cost debt issues with new debt sold at a lower rates.
The $350 million of new money will go principally toward improvements in the utility's gas and electric distribution and transmission systems.

Fitch Investors Service rated the offering AA-plus, and affirmed the utility's $2.5 billion outstanding electric and gas system revenue bonds at AA-plus. The rating agency also affirmed San Antonio's $300 million commercial paper program at F-1-plus."

"(City Public Service) is in the process of developing a comprehensive strategic plan to maintain its position as one of the lowest cost power suppliers in the southwestern U.S," a Fitch release said. "Elements of the plan include restructuring of rates, devising a wholesale and retail marketing plan, implementing a debt management program and reorganizing the company along functional lines."
Texas is currently in the early phases of wholesale electric industry deregulation, but is not under retail deregulation yet, Thomas said.
